criterion: Every command that takes a profile gives the same one-line reply for a name with a slash, space, dot or hyphen (a leading hyphen such as -x included), and the reply names the characters a profile name may hold.
evidence: tests/behaviour_coverage_test.py test_a_bad_name_gets_the_one_reply_from_every_command_gh_373 runs the real bin/ccmorph for 23 command forms (add, use, login, inspect, rm, mv twice, cred, run, config, get, set, context twice, probe three ways, quota twice, models, doctor, hop, _menu) against a/b, 'bad name', a.b, my-work, 日本語, a 300-letter name and active; test_a_leading_hyphen_word_gets_the_one_reply_gh_373 runs the same 23 forms with -x. Every row asserts one stderr line "ccmorph: invalid profile name '<name>': <reason>. Profiles: gw tok work" (the list only when profiles exist), empty stdout, unchanged state and an empty claude log. The sentence is profile.BadNameMsg; cli's badNameMsg appends the list once for every verb, including hop --slash. After `make shim`, `CCMORPH_LIB_DIR=$PWD/lib uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pytest-xdist --with pytest-timeout python -m pytest -q tests/behaviour_coverage_test.py -k gh_373` gives 200 passed.

criterion: No command answers a bad name with a usage line, with the prefix context-probe: or FAIL profile:, or with the words model listing requires an profile.
evidence: In the same tests stderr must equal the reply exactly and stdout must be empty, so no usage line, context-probe line or FAIL row can also appear. run -x is refused in the profile slot before the launch and probe -x before context-probe is spawned; the claude log must stay empty, proving no Claude was invoked. probe --bogus keeps context-probe's own usage error (tests/cli_messages_test.py test_probe_refuses_an_unknown_option_with_its_usage passed in the full run of behaviour_coverage_test.py + cli_messages_test.py: 366 passed). The old wordings are gone from the source: rg 'model listing requires an profile|profile: invalid profile name' cli returns nothing.

criterion: A person who types my-work learns from the reply that a hyphen is refused.
evidence: The my-work row of test_a_bad_name_gets_the_one_reply_from_every_command_gh_373 asserts exactly "ccmorph: invalid profile name 'my-work': a name may hold only A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _ (no hyphen, dot, slash or space). Profiles: gw tok work" for all 23 command forms, part of the 200 gh_373 cases that passed.

criterion: A name that is too long gets the same kind of one-line reply, with no file path in it.
evidence: The 'y' * 300 row of the same test asserts exactly "ccmorph: invalid profile name '<32 y>…': too long; at most 200 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _. Profiles: gw tok work" on one stderr line with empty stdout; profile.ValidName caps names at MaxNameLen = 200 and TestValidNameCapsTheLength proves 200 valid, 201 refused. The name is shown at most 32 runes, so no derived file path can appear.

criterion: The exit code for a bad name is the same in every command.
evidence: Every row of the bad-name and leading-hyphen tests asserts returncode == 1, including run -x and probe -x (previously 0 and 2). One form is deliberately different: the hidden `hop --slash` flag prints the same one-line reply on stdout and exits 0, because Claude Code renders a non-zero slash-command exit as 'Shell command failed' (#257); its test test_hop_to_a_wrong_name_inside_claude_answers_in_one_line asserts 0 for --slash and 1 for the `!` form, and passed (`CCMORPH_TEST_FILTER=test_hop_to_a_wrong_name_inside_claude_answers_in_one_line zsh tests/ccmorph_test.zsh`). Command form exits are uniform at 1.
